title: 一丛花令·伤高怀远几时穷
title_en: Yi Cong Hua Ling: When Will This Longing End
author: 张先

form.zh: 词，词牌《一丛花令》，双调七十八字
form.en: ci to the tune Yi Cong Hua Ling, 78 characters in two stanzas

text_note.zh: 古籍本作“沈恨”，“沈”是“沉”的古写法，读 chén。这里按通行本写作“沉恨”。
text_note.en: The old edition writes the word for deep in an older form that looks like the surname Shen. It is read chén; we use the common modern form.

readings.zh: “嘶骑”指嘶叫的马，“骑”按现在的规范读 qí。古代当名词“骑的马”讲时读 jì。
readings.en: Sī qí means a neighing horse. Today this character is read qí. In old usage, as a noun for a mount, it was read jì.

glosses.zh: 伤高怀远：登上高处，想念远方的人，心里伤感。
glosses.en: shāng gāo huái yuǎn: climbing high and longing for someone far away, feeling sad.

glosses.zh: 几时穷：什么时候才有尽头。穷，尽。
glosses.en: jǐ shí qióng: when will it ever end? Qióng means to come to an end.

glosses.zh: 无物似情浓：没有什么东西比爱情更浓烈。
glosses.en: wú wù sì qíng nóng: nothing is as strong as love.

glosses.zh: 千丝乱：千万条柳丝乱飘，像心里乱成一团的离愁。
glosses.en: qiān sī luàn: a thousand willow strands tossing about, like the tangle of sorrow at parting.

glosses.zh: 东陌：东边的小路，指当初分别的地方。
glosses.en: dōng mò: the eastern lane, where they parted.

glosses.zh: 飞絮蒙蒙：柳絮漫天飞舞，看不清楚。
glosses.en: fēi xù méng méng: willow fluff fills the air like a haze.

glosses.zh: 嘶骑：嘶叫着的马，指情郎骑的马。
glosses.en: sī qí: a neighing horse, the one her lover rode away on.

glosses.zh: 征尘：远行时马蹄扬起的尘土。
glosses.en: zhēng chén: the dust raised by hooves on a long journey.
láng zōng: a trace of her beloved.

glosses.zh: 双鸳：成双成对的鸳鸯，常用来比喻恩爱的夫妻。
glosses.en: shuāng yuān: a pair of mandarin ducks, a common symbol of a loving couple.

glosses.zh: 溶溶：水面宽阔、缓缓流动的样子。
glosses.en: róng róng: water broad and gently flowing.
xiǎo ráo: a small boat. Ráo means oar.

glosses.zh: 梯横：梯子横放着，收了起来，说明不会再有人上楼来了。
glosses.en: tī héng: the ladder lies flat, put away. No one will climb up to her now.

glosses.zh: 画阁：有彩绘装饰的楼阁。
帘栊：挂着帘子的窗户。栊，窗格。
glosses.en: lián lóng: a curtained window. Lóng means a window frame.

glosses.zh: 沉恨：深深的怨恨和愁苦。
glosses.en: chén hèn: deep sorrow and regret.

glosses.zh: 嫁东风：把自己嫁给春风。桃花杏花在春风里开放，又随春风飘去，好像嫁给了春风。
glosses.en: jià dōng fēng: to marry the east wind. Peach and apricot blossoms open in the spring wind and fly off with it, as if they had married it.

translation.zh: 登高怀念远方的人，这伤心什么时候才有尽头？
translation.en: Climbing high, longing for one far away, when will this sorrow end?

translation.zh: 世上没有什么比爱情更浓烈。
translation.en: Nothing in the world is as strong as love.

translation.zh: 离别的愁绪正像千万条柳丝乱飘，
translation.en: The grief of parting tosses like a thousand willow strands,

translation.zh: 更何况东边小路上，柳絮漫天飞舞。
translation.en: And on the eastern lane, willow fluff fills the air.

translation.zh: 他骑的马嘶叫着越走越远，
translation.en: His neighing horse moves farther and farther away;
The dust of his road keeps rising,

translation.zh: 到哪里才能找到情郎的踪影？
translation.en: Where can I find a trace of him now?

translation.zh: 池塘里一对对鸳鸯在宽阔的水面上游着，
translation.en: On the wide, gentle pond, mandarin ducks swim in pairs;

translation.zh: 南来北往的小船可以随意来去。
translation.en: Little boats come and go from south to north.

translation.zh: 黄昏以后，画阁的梯子已经收起横放，
translation.en: After dusk, the ladder to the painted pavilion lies put away;

translation.zh: 又只剩下斜斜的月光照着帘窗。
translation.en: Once again only the slanting moon shines on the curtained window.

translation.zh: 把这深深的愁恨仔细想一想，

translation.en: I am worse off than the peach and apricot blossoms,
For they at least know how to marry the east wind.

background.zh: 这首词写一位女子和情人分别后的思念。据宋人笔记《过庭录》记载，张先年轻时爱上一位住在池中小阁里的女子，两人只能在夜里靠梯子相见，后来不得不分开，他便写了这首词。这个故事是否属实已无法确定。又据说欧阳修很喜欢这首词的结尾，称张先为“桃杏嫁东风郎中”。
background.en: This lyric tells of a woman longing for her lover after they part. A Song dynasty book of notes says that as a young man, Zhang Xian loved a woman who lived in a small pavilion on a pond. They could only meet at night by a ladder, and later they had to part, so he wrote this lyric. Whether the story is true can no longer be known. It is also said that Ouyang Xiu loved the ending so much that he nicknamed Zhang Xian "the official of peach and apricot marrying the east wind".

author_note.zh: 张先（990—1078），字子野，乌程（今浙江湖州）人，北宋词人，做过都官郎中。他活了八十多岁，和晏殊、欧阳修、苏轼都有来往。他特别会写“影”，有“云破月来花弄影”等名句，人称“张三影”。他的词细腻柔美，常写男女之间的思念。
author_note.en: Zhang Xian (990–1078) came from Wucheng, today's Huzhou in Zhejiang. He was a Northern Song lyric poet and served as a court official. He lived past eighty and knew Yan Shu, Ouyang Xiu and Su Shi. He was especially good at writing about shadows, as in his famous line about clouds parting and flowers playing with their shadows in the moonlight, so people called him "Zhang of the Three Shadows". His lyrics are soft and delicate, often about longing between lovers.

appreciation.zh: 开头就是一声叹问：登高望远的伤心，什么时候才完？世上没有比爱情更浓的东西了。接着写眼前：柳丝乱飘，柳絮满天，就像她心里乱成一团的愁。她想起情郎骑马离开时，马越走越远，尘土一路扬起，最后连影子也找不到了。下片写她住的地方：池塘里鸳鸯成双，小船自由来往，可她却只能一个人待着。黄昏后梯子收起，只有斜月照着窗户，一天又一天都是这样。最后她忽发奇想：我还不如桃花杏花呢，它们至少还能嫁给春风！这个比喻又新奇又心酸，把她的孤单和怨恨说得淋漓尽致，成了千古名句。
appreciation.en: It opens with a sigh: when will the pain of gazing far for him ever end? Nothing is stronger than love. Then she looks around. Willow strands toss and fluff fills the sky, just like the tangle in her heart. She remembers him riding away. The horse went farther, the dust rose all along the road, and at last not even his shadow could be seen. The second stanza shows where she lives. Ducks swim in pairs on the pond and little boats come and go freely, yet she is alone. After dusk the ladder is put away and only the slanting moon shines on her window, day after day. At the end comes a strange, sudden thought: I am worse off than the peach and apricot blossoms, for at least they get to marry the spring wind! The image is fresh and heartbreaking. It says her loneliness and bitterness completely, and it became a famous line for all time.
